title: The Cockroach Janta Party protest in Delhi, 10 October 2026
about: A record of what was reported about the protest called for 10 October 2026 at Jantar Mantar and the police operation that prevented it. Every claim is attributed to whoever made it and linked to where it was reported. Nothing here is this site's own account of events: where accounts conflict, both are kept. Read on 2026-10-10 from search results and, from the evening, from the coverage wire's headlines; news sites could not be fetched in full from the editing environment, so wording follows the reports' published summaries.
demand: The resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which opposition parties say favours the ruling BJP; the Election Commission and government reject the allegation of voter manipulation.

noOfficialCount: No count published by Delhi Police itself was found. The Times of India's "more than 3,000", with 600 "with criminal records" held in preventive detention, reads like a police briefing, but its headline does not say whose figure it is.

restrictions.what: Prohibitory order under Section 163 BNSS in New Delhi district
restrictions.detail: Bars assemblies of five or more; protests not permitted at Jantar Mantar or anywhere else while it is in force, per DCP New Delhi Shrishti Pandey, who warned of legal action against unauthorised gatherings. Violations are prosecutable under Section 223 BNS, per the police's July advisory.

restrictions.what: Mobile data suspended within 4 km of the Janpath–Kartavya Path crossing
restrictions.detail: 10 pm on 9 October to 10 pm on 10 October, ordered by the Union Home Secretary under the Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules 2024 and Section 20(2)(b) of the Telecommunications Act 2023. About 2.5 times the area of the 1.5 km shutdown on 2 October. MediaNama reports the notice gives no grounds.

restrictions.what: Entry and exit suspended at 45 metro stations
restrictions.detail: Revised down from 57 planned, per The Indian Awaaz; Namo Bharat stations at Sarai Kale Khan and New Ashok Nagar closed until 10 pm. A single report; not confirmed against Delhi Metro's own notices.

restrictions.what: Security personnel deployed: 23,000 by one report, 35,000 by others
restrictions.detail: New Delhi district split into 20 security zones, per The Tribune; vehicle checkpoints on routes into the capital.

accounts.who: Sambit Patra, BJP national spokesperson
accounts.text: "India is calm and going ahead under good governance." What is happening at Jantar Mantar, seen on TV and a few social media handles, "is not India's story". He called the demonstrators "anarchic elements" and said their "flop show has been completely demolished".

accounts.who: Sambit Patra, BJP national spokesperson, as reported
accounts.text: Accused protesters of trying to bring the capital to a standstill and provoke arson and violence. A claim, not a finding; no report read for this record documented arson or violence on 10 October.

timeline.what: Abhijeet Dipke launches the Cockroach Janta Party.
The party demands Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over the voter-roll revision, and threatens nationwide protest from 2 October.
First protests of the new campaign. At least 11 metro stations around Jantar Mantar closed; a 1.5 km mobile-data shutdown.
Delhi Police: Section 163 still in force, no permission to protest. Nearly 1,000 had been detained on 2 October; at least three FIRs registered, naming no accused.
Police refuse permission for 10 October, saying the request came late. Dipke and other leaders detained on landing at Delhi airport, per the party.
Mobile-data suspension begins within 4 km of the Janpath–Kartavya Path crossing.

Central Delhi locked down: 45 metro stations shut, checkpoints on routes in. Detentions across the city, including about 200 in Connaught Place and lawyers marching from the Supreme Court; temporary holding centres, including stadiums, used.
Opposition leaders including Mamata Banerjee and Arvind Kejriwal detained near Jantar Mantar; reports count four former chief ministers among those held.
BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra: "India is calm". Congress, AAP, Amnesty, CPJ and bar associations condemn the detentions.
The party says it will resume the march; police have refused permission and issued a traffic advisory.
Congress plans its own march against the Chief Election Commissioner.
